questions.question_text:
The two broad areas of communication are
(A) Oral and written communication
(B) Verbal and written communication
(C) Verbal and Non-verbal communication
(D) Oral and Non-verbal communication
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The highest-level division of communication methods is between verbal (using words) and non-verbal (without words).

questions.question_text:
Select the most appropriate word: Nowadays, most children have a tendency to ________ the legitimate concerns of the parents.
(A) Disparage
(B) applaud
(C) reduce
(D) begrudge
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: 'Disparage' means to regard or represent as being of little worth, which contextually fits a negative tendency against legitimate concerns.

questions.question_text:
An example of asynchronous medium is
(A) Newspaper
(B) Film
(C) Television
(D) Radio
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Newspapers are printed and then read later at the reader's convenience, making it a classic asynchronous medium.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements BEST reflects the primary advantage of using visual aids in a presentation?
(A) They reduce the need for verbal explanation entirely.
(B) They guarantee audience agreement with the presenter.
(C) They enhance comprehension and retention by appealing to multiple senses.
(D) They allow the presenter to speak less and avoid preparation.
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Visual aids reinforce spoken words visually, significantly improving the audience's ability to understand and remember the content.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statement is true about communication?
(A) 50% of impact is determined by body language
(B) 36% by voice tonality
(C) 7% by the words
(D) 58% by kinesics
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: According to Mehrabian's rule of personal communication, 7% of meaning is communicated through spoken words.

questions.question_text:
If the marketing manager discusses about the present state of the work with the finance manager, it will be the case of ________
(A) upward communication
(B) downward communication
(C) horizontal communication
(D) diagonal communication
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Communication between individuals at the same hierarchical level (manager to manager) is horizontal communication.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is the process in which the receiver interprets and understands the message?
(A) Encoding
(B) Decoding
(C) Channel
(D) Source
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Decoding is the action performed by the receiver to extract meaning from the sender's encoded message.

questions.question_text:
________ listening is also known as critical listening.
(A) Active
(B) Empathetic
(C) Appreciative
(D) Evaluative
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Evaluative listening involves making judgments and critically analyzing the speaker's message, identical to critical listening.

questions.question_text:
Choose the correct verb forms for the following sentence:
The theatre company ________ a grant of £6.000 and it ________ a further £2.000 from elsewhere now.
(A) is given / has been seeking
(B) will be given / seeks
(C) was given / has sought
(D) has been given / is seeking
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: 'has been given' refers to a recently completed action relevant to the present, while 'is seeking' matches the present continuous cue 'now'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate connectives:
We live in the same building; ________, we hardly see each other.
(A) Furthermore
(B) However
(C) Therefore
(D) Hence
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: The sentence contains a contrast between living in the same building and hardly seeing each other. 'However' is the appropriate contrastive connective.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with correct form of verb that agrees with the subject:
A number of my friends ________ riding bicycles, but neither my brother nor my sister ________ a bicycle.
(A) love / owns
(B) loves / own
(C) love /own
(D) loves / owning
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('love'). 'Neither... nor' with singular nouns takes a singular verb ('owns').

questions.question_text:
Change the following sentence into passive voice:
I remember my sister taking me to the museum.
(A) I remember myself being taken to the museum by my sister.
(B) I remember being taken to the museum by my sister.
(C) I remember taken to the museum by my sister.
(D) I remember I was taken to the museum by my sister.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Using 'being taken' properly converts the gerund 'taking' into the passive structure while maintaining the meaning of the original sentence.

questions.question_text:
Why is it important to use standardized symbols in flowcharts?
(A) To make the flowchart visually appealing
(B) To represent artistic creativity
(C) To ensure clarity and understanding
(D) To showcase individual style preferences
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Standardized symbols act as a universal language, allowing anyone familiar with flowcharts to read and understand the process clearly.
questions.chapter: Unit 2 - English: The Language of Science & Technology

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is an example of "flaming" in online communication?
(A) Complimenting someone's work in a group chat
(B) Sending a friendly greeting to a new member of an online community
(C) Sharing helpful resources with colleagues
(D) Engaging in a heated argument with insults and personal
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Flaming is Internet slang for hostile and insulting interaction between internet users.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is an example of synchronous communication?
(A) Email
(B) Text messaging
(C) Forums
(D) Video conferencing
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Video conferencing allows for immediate, real-time response from participants.

questions.question_text:
Choose the sentence with the correct question tag.
She went to the library yesterday, ________?
(A) didn't she
(B) did she
(C) does she
(D) is she
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The main clause is positive and in the past tense ('went'), so the question tag must be negative and use 'did'.

questions.question_text:
What is the primary purpose of a letter of motivation in a job application?
(A) To provide a summary of qualifications.
(B) To request an interview.
(C) To explain why you are the right candidate for the position.
(D) To list previous work experiences.
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: While resumes list experiences, motivation letters specifically bridge the gap by explaining the applicant's intent and fit for the role.

questions.question_text:
In critical reasoning, what does it mean to "analyze the text"?
(A) Summarizing the main points.
(B) Criticizing the font style and size used.
(C) Ignoring the content and focusing on grammar.
(D) Identifying the author's argument and evidence.
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Critical analysis involves deconstructing a text to find its core arguments and evaluating the strength of the supporting evidence.

questions.question_text:
Find out the grammatical error in the following sentence:
The captain along with his team / are practicing very hard / for the / forth coming matches.
(A) The captain along with his team
(B) are practicing very hard
(C) for the
(D) forth coming matches.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Phrases like 'along with' do not change the number of the subject. The subject 'The captain' is singular, so the verb should be 'is practicing'.

questions.question_text:
Identify the degree of comparison for the following sentence:
The roads of Chandigarh are much wider than the other cities of India.
(A) Comparative
(B) Positive
(C) Superlative
(D) Negative
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The adjective 'wider' and the use of 'than' denote a comparative degree.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following activities is an example of extensive reading?
(A) Reading a scientific article to extract key findings.
(B) Reading a novel for pleasure and general understanding.
(C) Reading a legal document to understand specific clauses.
(D) Reading a technical manual to learn specific procedures.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Extensive reading involves reading longer texts largely for general understanding and enjoyment.

questions.question_text:
Change the following direct speech into indirect speech:
The doctor said to the patient, "How do you feel now? Has the pain gone down?"
(A) The doctor asked the patient how he had felt when the pain was gone.
(B) The doctor asked the patient how he is feeling now and if the pain has gone down.
(C) The doctor asked the patient how he felt then and if the pain had gone down.
(D) The doctor asked the patient how he was feeling then and if the pain was down.
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: In reported speech, present tense verbs shift to past tense ('feel' -> 'felt', 'Has... gone' -> 'had gone'), and 'now' changes to 'then'.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is typically included in an agenda for a meeting?
(A) Detailed meeting minutes
(B) Background information on attendees.
(C) Personal opinions of the meeting organizer.
(D) Items to be discussed and their respective time slots.
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: An agenda outlines the schedule of topics or items to be addressed during a meeting.

questions.question_text:
An ________ report is a form of report in which reporters deal with a single topic of interest, such as serious crimes, political corruption, or corporate wrongdoing.
(A) investigative
(B) analytical
(C) interrogative
(D) Enquiry
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Investigative reporting requires uncovering deep facts about hidden or complex issues like corruption.

questions.question_text:
________ of impact is determined by body language-postures, gestures, and eye contact.
(A) 70%
(B) 55%
(C) 38%
(D) 7%
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: According to the 55/38/7 rule of communication, 55% of the impact is delivered through non-verbal cues (body language).

questions.question_text:
In which of following, the listener puts himself in place of the speaker?
(A) Empathetic listening
(B) Appreciative listening
(C) Combative listening
(D) Attentive listening
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Empathetic listening requires the listener to understand the speaker's emotional state by putting themselves in the speaker's shoes.

questions.question_text:
Choose the correct verb forms for the following sentence:
Arun was very upset yesterday because he ________ that he ________ his wallet.
(A) realized/lost
(B) realizes/has lost
(C) has realized/ lost
(D) realized/ had lost
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: The first blank needs the simple past 'realized' for yesterday's action. The second action occurred prior to the realization, requiring the past perfect 'had lost'.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate Conjunctions / Connectives:
________ you work out regularly, you will not see any results.
(A) Although
(B) Because
(C) Unless
(D) Though
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: 'Unless' introduces the condition required to avoid the negative result.

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate synonym for 'translucent'.
(A) Opaque
(B) Vague
(C) Timeless
(D) Transparent
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Transparent is the closest synonym provided, as both relate to allowing light to pass through.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT a rule of précis writing?
(A) Always have a heading
(B) Use as extensive vocabulary as possible
(C) Remove any irrelevant information present in the original passage
(D) Do not use any short forms or abbreviations
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Précis writing prioritizes clarity and simplicity; excessive or complex vocabulary violates this rule.

questions.question_text:
Choose the sentence with the correct question tag.
Swastik attends the class regularly, ________?
(A) did he
(B) Has he
(C) doesn't he
(D) does he
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: A positive present-tense statement with an action verb ('attends') requires the negative tag 'doesn't he'.

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate antonym for 'abstain'.
(A) Regress
(B) Imbibe
(C) Restrain
(D) Indulge
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: Abstain means to hold oneself back from an action or pleasure. Its opposite is to indulge.

questions.question_text:
Typing in all capitals in electronic communication means ________.
(A) you are happy.
(B) you are shouting.
(C) it's okay to forward this message to others.
(D) this message is very important.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: In standard internet etiquette (netiquette), ALL CAPS is interpreted as shouting.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is not a netiquette guideline?
(A) Respect others' privacy
(B) Respond to emails and texts promptly
(C) If you wouldn't say it face to face, say it online.
(D) Choose friends wisely
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The standard guideline is the opposite: Do NOT say things online that you wouldn't say to someone's face.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT a parallel sentence?
(A) Mohan and Ramu are planning to carpool to the party, to dance, and to attend the after party.
(B) Stephen's mom complained that he had too many bad habits: he would never clean up his room, brush his teeth, or vacuuming the house.
(C) Eleanor spends her time reading, listening to music, and working at the mall.
(D) Bob had an active life: he swam twenty laps, ran five miles, and lifted weights every day.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Option B mixes base verbs ('clean', 'brush') with a gerund ('vacuuming'), breaking grammatical parallel structure.

questions.question_text:
Find out the grammatical error in the following sentence:
John is / one of the Students, / who is dependable / in all the circumstances
(A) John is
(B) one of the Students
(C) who is dependable
(D) in all the circumstances
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'Students', so the verb should be plural 'are dependable'.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is NOT an example of acronym?
(A) UNO
(B) SIM
(C) RADAR
(D) ZIP
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Acronyms are pronounced as a single word (SIM, RADAR, ZIP). UNO is typically pronounced letter-by-letter, making it an initialism.

questions.question_text:
________ is a process of analyzing, interpreting, and evaluating.
(A) Skimming
(B) Scanning
(C) Critical reading
(D) Through reading
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Critical reading requires deep mental engagement, where the reader analyzes and evaluates the text rather than just understanding the surface meaning.

questions.question_text:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate verb forms:
A regiment of soldiers ________ deployed for election duty.
(A) are
(B) is
(C) had
(D) were
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: 'Regiment' acts as a singular collective noun representing the group as a single unit.

questions.question_text:
Identify the degree of comparison for the following sentence:
In mountain regions, day travel is better than night travel.
(A) Comparative
(B) Positive
(C) Superlative
(D) Negative
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The word 'better' coupled with 'than' indicates a comparison between two subjects.

questions.question_text:
Change the following sentence into passive voice:
She was crafting an antique.
(A) An antique is being crafted by her.
(B) An antique has been crafted by her.
(C) An antique was been crafted by her.
(D) An antique was being crafted by her.
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: The past continuous active tense ('was crafting') correctly transitions to the past continuous passive tense ('was being crafted').

questions.question_text:
Change the following direct speech into indirect speech:
She said, 'Will you come for the party?'
(A) She said we would come for the party.
(B) She asked whether we would come for the party.
(C) She exclaimed we will come for the party.
(D) She asked whether you will come for the party.
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Yes/no questions are reported using 'if' or 'whether', and 'will' changes to its past equivalent 'would'.
